purpose: Brinzolamide eye drops are used to lower the pressure inside your eye. It is prescribed for conditions like glaucoma or ocular hypertension, where the pressure in your eye is too high. Keeping eye pressure under control helps protect your vision over time.
how_it_works: Your eye constantly makes a fluid called aqueous humor. Brinzolamide works by blocking an enzyme called carbonic anhydrase, which slows down how much of this fluid your eye produces. Less fluid means less pressure building up inside your eye.
common_side_effects: You may notice a temporary blurry vision right after putting in the drops — this is normal and usually clears up quickly. Other common effects include a mild bitter or unusual taste in your mouth, mild eye discomfort or stinging, and eye redness. Some people also notice a feeling like something is in their eye.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to sulfa drugs, as brinzolamide is related to that drug family and could cause a reaction. Do not use it if you have severe kidney problems. If you wear soft contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. Always tell your doctor about all other eye drops or medications you are taking.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one drop in the affected eye or eyes three times a day. Try to space your doses evenly throughout the day, such as morning, afternoon, and evening. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 to 10 minutes between different drops.
